documents.unit: AI at UC (AI Enablement Community of Practice)
documents.title: Guidelines on AI use
documents.stance_why: The guidelines say they are "not intended as a list of restrictions, but as a compass" and tell students to "check with faculty members" and "review course syllabi", so no default allow or ban is set and the decision goes to instructors; the only firm rules concern data.
documents.summary: Short university guidelines on responsible AI use: sign into UC-licensed tools, use only public data, follow the code of conduct. Students are sent to instructors and syllabi for course rules. A brief research note asks investigators to indicate AI use in proposals.

units.why: The opening frames the guidelines as "not intended as a list of restrictions, but as a compass", which sets purpose and principles for AI use institution-wide, so P56 (framework) with informs modality; P56 fits better than P87 because it states principles, not benefits.
units.anchor: not intended as a list of restrictions, but as a compass
units.frag_end: ethical and practical landscape of AI

units.why: The text names "academic integrity, intellectual curiosity, and human-centered responsibility" as the pillars, a statement of principles for the whole framework, so P56.
units.anchor: built on the pillars of academic integrity, intellectual curiosity, and human-centered responsibility
units.frag_start: It is built on the pillars

units.why: "As this field evolves, so will our approach, and we invite you to be a part" says the guidelines will change and invites feedback, which is exactly P54.
units.anchor: As this field evolves, so will our approach

units.why: The sentence "Sign into UC-licensed tools with your UC credentials" directs users to licensed tools for privacy and security; it is institution-wide, not one course, so P92 rather than P17.
units.anchor: Sign into UC-licensed tools with your UC credentials
units.policy: Sign into UC-licensed tools with your UC credentials

units.why: The licensing agreements "offer privacy-protected access to approved AI and Generative AI tools", a fact about approved tools and privacy that supports the licensed-tool rule; P92 (approved tools) fits.
units.anchor: privacy-protected access to approved AI and Generative AI tools

units.why: "Verify that the data you intend to interact with is classified as Public" is a data-protection duty before using AI, so P50 with must modality as the text uses imperative "Verify".
units.anchor: Verify that the data you intend to interact with is classified

units.why: "Neither controlled nor restricted data are approved for use in AI tools" bans a category of data from AI tools; this is protection of confidential data (P50), not a ban on uploading course materials (P49).
units.anchor: Neither controlled nor restricted data are approved for use in AI tools

units.why: "When in doubt, seek guidance from the Office of Information Security" names an office to ask about data classification; it is an ask-when-unsure rule (P10) though about data, so a fit_note is added.
units.anchor: When in doubt, seek guidance from the
units.fit_note: Asks users to consult the Information Security office about data classification, not the instructor about allowed AI use.

units.why: "UC student directory data is not approved for use in AI tools" bars one named data type from AI tools, so P50 protecting personal data.
units.anchor: UC student directory data is not approved for use in AI tools

units.why: "exercise caution to avoid inadvertently sharing personal information" tells users to avoid exposing personal data even when it is public; personal-data protection, P50.
units.anchor: exercise caution to avoid inadvertently sharing personal information
units.frag_start: Even when dealing with public data,

units.why: "complies with legal requirements, copyright laws, and ethical standards" requires AI use to follow law and ethics; P77 (comply with existing law) fits better than P52 because it is a general compliance duty, not about ownership of output.
units.anchor: Ensure that your use of AI technology and public data complies with legal requirements

units.why: "Communicate with your instructors about the acceptability and appropriate use of AI" tells students to ask instructors first, matching P10.
units.anchor: Communicate with your instructors about the acceptability and appropriate use of AI

units.why: "Faculty members can provide clear guidance about how these tools may or may not fit into their learning objectives" leaves the decision to instructors; P04 as the instructor-sets-rule type, though it also ties the decision to learning objectives (P83).
units.anchor: how these tools may or may not fit into their learning objectives
units.fit_note: Also ties the decision to learning objectives and evaluation criteria (P83).

units.why: "Carefully read the syllabi for each of your courses at the beginning of the term" makes students responsible for finding each course's AI rules, which is P78.
units.anchor: Carefully read the syllabi for each of your courses at the beginning of the term

units.why: "reach out to your instructor if you're unsure" tells students to ask the instructor when the syllabus does not settle a question about AI, matching P10.
units.anchor: reach out to your instructor if you're unsure

units.why: "should align with the UC Student Code of Conduct" says AI use must follow the existing integrity code; P77 (comply with existing university policy) rather than P36 because it does not say misuse is misconduct.
units.anchor: should align with the
units.frag_start: The responsible use of technology, including

units.why: "Investigators are encouraged to indicate in the project description the extent to which, if any, generative AI technology was used" asks researchers to disclose AI use in proposals; research rule, P62 over P24 because it governs grants.
units.anchor: the extent to which, if any, generative AI technology was used
units.fit_note: Also a disclosure request (P24) for AI use in proposals.

units.why: The NSF/NIH reviewer line tells reviewers to "pay attention" to the funders' rules on AI in peer review, deferring to funder rules; P62.
units.anchor: If you serve as an NSF or NIH reviewer, please pay attention

units.why: The linked notice "Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence Technologies Prohibited in NIH Peer Review Process" points to a funder prohibition on AI in peer review that the university relays; P62.
units.anchor: Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence Technologies Prohibited in NIH Peer Review Process

documents.title: AI Applicable Policies
documents.stance_why: The page only lists existing policies (data governance, acceptable use, conduct) that apply to AI and sets no AI stance of its own, so teaching decisions are left to other documents.
documents.summary: Lists existing university policies (information security, data governance, acceptable use, accessibility, security review, student and employee conduct, export control) said to apply to AI. It adds no new AI-specific rules except bans on conflict of interest and harassment through AI.

units.why: "required to comply with these policies while utilizing AI" makes UC information security policy bind AI use; P77.
units.anchor: All persons with access to UC digital infrastructure, data, or services are required to comply
units.frag_end: while utilizing AI at the university.

units.why: "The Data Governance and Classification Policy is applicable when using AI" says an existing data policy governs AI use; P77, with privacy as topic.
units.anchor: The Data Governance and Classification Policy is applicable when using AI
units.frag_start: The University of Cincinnati uses a variety

units.why: The explanation that "federal and state laws require that the university must limit access to certain categories of data to protect the privacy" gives the legal basis for data protection; P50 informs.
units.anchor: federal and state laws require that the university must limit access

units.why: "The Acceptable Use policy is applicable to the use of AI" binds AI use to the acceptable-use policy; P77.
units.anchor: The Acceptable Use policy is applicable to the use of AI

units.why: The accessibility policy sets standards "regarding the design, development, acquisition and use of electronic and information technology resources, including AI"; accessibility of AI tools is P97.
units.anchor: accessibility standards and expectations regarding the design, development, acquisition and use

units.why: Information security risk assessments "are necessary to identify and document information security risk" for IT including AI, i.e., review of AI tools before adoption; P65.
units.anchor: Information security risk assessments

units.why: "required to comply with these policies while utilizing AI at the university" makes conduct policies bind students and employees using AI; P77.
units.anchor: Students and employees who access UC digital infrastructure, data, or services are required to comply

units.why: "The Student Code of Conduct is applicable to the use of AI" says student AI misuse falls under the code, whose procedures and sanctions then apply; P77 because the text does not itself call misuse misconduct.
units.anchor: The Student Code of Conduct is applicable to the use of AI

units.why: "The use of AI must comply with Export Control Regulations" for students binds AI use to export law; P77.
units.anchor: The use of AI must comply with Export Control Regulations
units.frag_start: All students, volunteers, and visitors engaged

units.why: "AI may not be used in a manner that creates a conflict of interest" bans a conduct harm by employees; P74 (conduct rules against improper AI use) fits closest.
units.anchor: AI may not be used in a manner that creates a conflict of interest
units.frag_start: The UC Conflict of Interest policy
units.fit_note: Bans a conflict-of-interest use rather than deception or malice.

units.why: "AI may not be used to engage in any form of harassment" is a ban on harmful AI use, P74 (harass).
units.anchor: AI may not be used to engage in any form of harassment
units.frag_start: All employees are required to comply

units.why: For employees, "The use of AI must comply with Export Regulations" binds faculty and staff AI use to export law; P77.
units.anchor: The use of AI must comply with Export
units.frag_start: All faculty, staff, volunteers, and visitors engaged

units.why: "may receive disciplinary action, up to and including termination, for conduct and/or rules violations" states employee sanctions under the conduct policy; it is about general conduct, so P77 with a fit_note.
units.anchor: An employee may receive disciplinary action, up to and including termination
units.fit_note: States sanctions for employees under the conduct rule, not AI-specific.

notes: Coder A. Two university-layer documents only; no teaching-specific AI rules beyond delegating to instructors and syllabi.
